utterance: Hello Graham, I'm the doctor. You look unwell, so we'll assess this straight away. Is the indigestion happening right now, where do you feel it, and what time did it start?
reply: Yes, it is still there now. Right in the middle, behind the breastbone. Bit up into the throat. It started about seven this morning, and it has been going the whole time. It is like a heaviness. Like indigestion but... heavier. Sort of a weight sitting on my chest.

utterance: This could be a heart attack rather than indigestion. Please stay resting here; don't walk or drive. We're arranging urgent help while checking your heart. Does the heaviness spread to your arms, jaw or back, and have you had sweating, breathlessness, nausea or faintness?
reply: Now you mention it, my jaw's a bit achy, and my left arm feels heavy, but not my back. I've been sweating like anything, thought it was just hot. I am a bit short of breath, yeah, and it is hard to get a proper breath in. I feel a bit sick, though I haven't vomited. I was a bit light-headed getting out of the car, but I didn't pass out.

awards.label: Whether the discomfort spreads or travels anywhere (arms, jaw, neck, back)
Red flag: Sweating or clamminess with the pain
Red flag: Dizziness, light-headedness or fainting

result: Sinus bradycardia 54/min. ST elevation 2–3 mm in II, III and aVF. Reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL. No LBBB.

utterance: An emergency ambulance is being called now. Have you ever had an allergy to aspirin, any recent serious bleeding, or been told not to take aspirin? Have you taken anything for this today?
reply: No allergies that I know of, I've had Disprin before, no problems. No recent bleeding, and I don't take aspirin or anything like that. I haven't taken anything for this today, but... yeah, took one of those Viagra tablets last night. Don't tell the missus I told you.

awards.label: Red flag: Taking any other medicines or tablets, beyond the regular ones (e.g. occasional, from the chemist, a friend or online)

dose: 300 mg dispersed in water or chewed

result: No ST elevation in V4R. No evidence of right ventricular involvement.

utterance: The heart tracing shows a heart attack affecting the bottom part of your heart. You need emergency hospital treatment to open the blocked artery. We're giving aspirin now to help stop the clot growing. Thank you for telling me about Viagra—it's confidential, and important because the chest-pain medicine called GTN can dangerously drop your blood pressure after Viagra, so we will not give it. What time did you take it, and was it definitely Viagra rather than Cialis or another tablet?
reply: It was definitely Viagra, around ten last night. Bloody hell, a heart attack? Is this going to kill me?

finding: Heart sounds dual, soft S4. No murmur. No rub.

utterance: This is serious, but getting treatment quickly makes a big difference. You did the right thing coming in. We will stay with you and monitor you until the ambulance team takes over. How strong is the pain out of ten? Did it come on suddenly at its worst, with any tearing pain into your back? Are you taking any blood thinners or any other medicines apart from your blood pressure and cholesterol tablets and the Viagra?
reply: I don't know, maybe a six? It's more heavy than sore. It crept up on me, and nothing like that. No blood thinners. I take Perindopril five milligrams daily and Atorvastatin forty milligrams daily.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Sudden severe tearing or ripping pain

utterance: Graham, we'll keep you resting, with your heart rhythm and blood pressure watched closely and emergency equipment ready. Your oxygen level is normal, so you don't need extra oxygen right now. We'll hand over directly to the ambulance team: symptoms began at 7 am, the tracing shows a heart attack, aspirin has been given, and you took Viagra at 10 pm, so no GTN. You need urgent transfer to a hospital that can open the artery, usually with a small tube and a stent. We won't delay transfer for blood tests. Tell me straight away if the heaviness worsens, you feel faint, or your breathing gets worse. Would you like us to contact your wife?

We'll contact your wife and tell her you need urgent hospital treatment for a heart attack. We'll keep the Viagra information private from her, but share it with the treating team for your safety. I'm asking the clinic team to stay with you, arrange a vein line for emergency medicines, and have the defibrillator ready while we wait for the ambulance. Please don't get up, even to go to the toilet.
reply: Bloody hell, all this fuss over a bit of indigestion. Can't I just go home after the hospital?

utterance: I know it feels like indigestion, but the heart tracing shows a heart attack. Going home now would be unsafe: the heart can develop a dangerous rhythm or become too weak to pump properly. You will need urgent treatment and monitoring in hospital, and the hospital team will tell you when it's safe to go home. We'll stay with you until the ambulance arrives.
reply: Alright, if you say so. Just don't let the blokes at work find out about this.

utterance: Your medical information is confidential—we won't tell your workmates. Right now our priority is getting you safely to the heart specialists as quickly as possible.
reply: Good. Just get me sorted out then.

quotes.ideal_2: We will stay with you and monitor you until the ambulance team takes over.
